requirements.statement: Render the supplied label visibly and as the Card aria-label; loading marks the Card aria-busy.
Format numeric values with Intl.NumberFormat using en-GB and the supplied format options; render string values as supplied. Append a truthy unit without calculating or converting the value.
Omit comparison when delta is undefined or nonfinite. A finite delta renders a signed percent with at most one fractional digit and the supplied comparison label.
Arrow direction follows delta sign, but success/destroy treatment follows trendIsPositive when given and otherwise whether delta is positive. Zero is always neutral and described as unchanged.

Set trendIsPositive when a decrease is beneficial or when product semantics differ from positive-is-good. Supply delta as an already-computed percentage; the card does not derive it from value or prior data.
Include screen-reader text describing unchanged, favorable or unfavorable change alongside the signed delta. Decorative direction arrows are aria-hidden.

With sparkline supplied, bar selects MiniBarChart and other variants select Sparkline. Explicit intent controls the chart accent independently of favorability; otherwise neutral uses function and nonneutral uses the derived trend.
While loading, retain the label and render a named status with skeletons instead of value, chart and comparison. Do not leave stale metric content presented as the current value in that branch.
Supply accurate deltaLabel and sparklineLabel when the data is not the default previous/last 24 hours. Model missing or failed metric data explicitly; there is no dedicated error or no-data prop.

MetricCard-owned typography and spacing use data-display tokens even though its API family name includes charts. Card, Skeleton and nested chart components retain surface, feedback and data-viz ownership respectively.

limitations: MetricCard is distinct from ChartMetricCard and does not provide a detailed chart, calculation engine or data-fetch lifecycle.
The value is not normalized for nonfinite numbers; callers must choose truthful missing/error content.
Default comparison and trend labels assume a 24-hour period and must be overridden when inaccurate.

document.purpose: Render a compact noninteractive visual summary of a nonnegative numeric series with an accessible text label.
document.behaviorProvider: Native SVG geometry and Aegis data normalization, with shared Skeleton for loading.

component: bounded dimensions and normalized samples
compact SVG geometry and image label
loading and empty replacements
host: valid series meaning, scale expectations and accessible summary
finite intended dimensions and nonnegative data domain

requirements.statement: Map each nonfinite sample to zero and clamp each finite negative sample to zero before computing geometry or the default label. Do not claim preservation of signed data.
Use group-token default dimensions when absent or nonfinite and clamp finite dimensions to token minimums. Explicit dimensions determine the SVG viewBox and empty/loading footprint.
Loading takes precedence over data and returns a named status containing a Skeleton. An empty nonloading series returns a dash image labeled with label or No activity data.
A populated SVG uses role=img and label when supplied; otherwise describe bucket count, latest normalized value and peak. No title, axis labels or exact-value table is added.
For line/area a single sample is a centered dot; multiple samples form a line and area adds a baseline closure. Bars use zero-based normalized heights relative to a peak of at least one.

Treat line/area geometry as a compact locally normalized trend, not a shared quantitative axis. Supply a detailed chart or exact-data alternative when users must compare magnitudes across independent sparklines.

Supply a label that states the actual quantity, time range and useful trend summary when the generic event-bucket text would be inaccurate. Decorative use and surrounding redundancy require an explicit accessibility decision.

The implementation adds no animation, focus target or pointer interaction. General SVG props are forwarded only in the populated branch, so callers must not rely on those props being retained for loading or empty replacements.
Generate a per-instance id for the AI gradient so multiple sparklines do not intentionally share a gradient definition. Other intents render with their group-token currentColor.
Use data-viz group tokens for palette, dimensions and geometry defaults; keep nested Skeleton styling in its feedback group. Do not bypass group ownership through caller style overrides.

limitations: Negative values are clipped and nonfinite values become zero; this is not a signed or missing-data-preserving chart.
There is no interactive tooltip, keyboard exploration or exact-value table.
Generic SVG props including className/style are not applied to the empty or loading replacement nodes.
Explicit labels can override the generic data summary and therefore must remain truthful.

document.purpose: Browse a supplied local dataset with sortable columns, row selection, optional details, local pagination and optional virtualization.
anatomy: data rows with optional selection and expansion controls
states: column sorted, resized, reordered or pinned
document.behaviorProvider: TanStack Table and Virtual provide row models and measured rendering; Aegis implements row keyboard handling and composes shared Checkbox, DropdownMenu and Pagination controls.

requirements.statement: Supply stable unique getRowId values and meaningful rowLabel values; selection, expansion, keyed rendering and focus restoration use those identities. Keep custom cell controls independently named.

selectedRowIds controls the selection when supplied; otherwise defaultSelectedRowIds initializes internal selection. Selection changes emit all selected ids and only matching row objects from the currently supplied data.

A controlled host must feed accepted selectedRowIds back and decide whether ids absent from current data remain selected. Bulk-action row objects cover only records present in data, not unavailable server records.

The supplied data is locally sorted and paginated by default. Pagination derives its total from data.length and clamps a rendered page after data shrinks; pagination=false presents the supplied rows without local page slicing. pageSize initializes internal page state rather than controlling later page-size changes.

Loading replaces body rows with skeletons and marks the grid busy; otherwise a truthy error replaces rows with the error EmptyState and optional retry action; otherwise zero displayed rows renders the empty state. Loading disables pagination but is not a blanket lock on every toolbar or header control.

When a key originates on the row itself, Up/Down/Home/End move row focus, Enter invokes onRowClick, Space toggles enabled selection, and Right/Left expand or collapse eligible details. Events from nested controls do not execute those row shortcuts.
A row click invokes onRowClick only outside recognized interactive descendants and when no text selection exists. The host must supply actual navigation or detail-opening behavior.

When supplying renderToolbar, render its selectionActions in the intended selection mode and connect density and visibility through the supplied toolbar API. Custom bulk actions must implement their real operations and call clear when appropriate.

Column menus provide pinning, sorting, hiding and movement alternatives to drag; movement stays within a pinned or unpinned group, and the built-in visibility controls preserve at least one visible data column. Resize handles support Arrow keys, Shift larger steps, Home/End bounds and Enter autosize.

Virtualization is requested explicitly or defaults on above 200 supplied records, and is inactive during loading/error or with no entries. Row focus scrolls the target into view; detail rows have separate measured entries. Resize observers, drag listeners and resize listeners are cleaned up on unmount.

Provide the complete local result set and apply filters before passing data. Fetching, error recovery, remote pagination, authorization and persistence of user column preferences are host responsibilities; the grid does not implement those services.

Use data-display group tokens for grid-owned visuals and density; nested Checkbox, DropdownMenu, EmptyState and Pagination retain their own groups. Preserve dimensions across the four theme/mode mappings and verify the actual scroll container.

limitations: This baseline covers DataGrid, not the record-specific DataGridPresentation demonstration or every data-grid cell family.
Sorting, expansion, column state and pagination are initialized internally; they are not a general externally controlled or server-side grid protocol.
Row-oriented keyboard handling is not an editable spreadsheet or full two-dimensional cell navigation model.
No browser run, visual acceptance or comprehensive accessibility certification is implied by these source-backed requirements.

entries.name: SearchInput
entries.summary: A searchable text field that separates immediate draft changes from debounced search requests.

document.purpose: Capture a search query immediately and optionally emit a debounced search callback.
document.behaviorProvider: Composition of TextInput with a React-managed debounce timer; native input behavior remains with TextInput.

component: Immediate query entry and native search semantics
Cancellation of superseded pending timers
Clear action and display-only shortcut hint
host: Result computation, fetching and asynchronous race handling
Accessible query name and result announcements
Controlled updates, shortcut registration and submission policy

requirements.statement: Compose TextInput with type search, a decorative Search icon and a forwarded input ref. The type, prefix and suffix are owned by SearchInput rather than exposed as replacement props.

Use controlled value or local text initialized from defaultValue. onValueChange is called immediately for edits, and the inherited native onChange remains immediate; debounce applies only to onSearch.
For a query different from the last emitted query, schedule onSearch after Math.max(0, debounceMs), defaulting debounceMs to 250 milliseconds.
Cancel the pending timer when query or debounceMs changes and on unmount. Read the current onSearch callback through a ref when the timer fires.
Initialize lastEmitted from the initial query so mounting alone does not emit onSearch. A later controlled value change follows the same debounce path as a user edit.
Preserve TextInput labeling, Field metadata, native form attributes, disabled/readOnly behavior and clearing. clearable defaults true and the clear label defaults to Clear search.
When passing value, accept edits by updating it through the immediate change callback. Keep the input draft distinct from any delayed search results.

Implement result filtering or requests, loading/error/empty states and result announcements. Cancel or ignore stale asynchronous results in the host; clearing a pending timer cannot cancel an onSearch request that already began.
Give the search input an accessible name and implement any advertised keyboard shortcut in the owning page. shortcut renders a kbd hint only; SearchInput does not register a shortcut handler.
Keep SearchInput-owned styling in the input group and preserve the nested TextInput behavior and keyboard focus treatment across modes.

limitations: Debounce cancellation applies to pending timers, not network requests, promises or search side effects already started.
No initial search, Enter-to-search override, result list, loading indicator or search service is supplied by this component.
TextInput native-form reset limitations also apply to the locally stored SearchInput query. Existing linked checks are bounded story assertions, not certification.

entries.name: SegmentedControl
entries.summary: A compact, mutually exclusive choice implemented with native radio inputs.

document.purpose: Select one value from a short related option set using a labeled native radio group.
document.behaviorProvider: Native HTML fieldset, legend and radio inputs with React state and input-focus modality tracking.

component: Native radio grouping and label association
Initial default selection and value-change notifications
Group/option disabled states and presentation flags
host: Meaningful group and option labels
Stable option identities and controlled state
Application effects and any stable form serialization

requirements.statement: Render a fieldset with a visually hidden legend from label. Render each option as a labeled radio and use one generated useId name for the native radio group.
Initialize local state from defaultValue when supplied, otherwise from the first non-disabled option, otherwise the empty string. Display value instead when a controlled value is supplied.
On a radio change, update local state only when value is undefined and notify onValueChange with that option value. Set each radio checked state by equality with the selected string.
Disable the fieldset for a disabled group and individual radio inputs for option.disabled. Expose disabled/selected attributes on option wrappers for their corresponding styles.
Keep native radio keyboard behavior and focus tracking. The keyboard story selects Monthly and uses ArrowRight to check Quarterly.
Expose size, fullWidth and wrap as presentation attributes while retaining the same fieldset/radio interaction model.

Supply unique stable option values and meaningful option labels. Keep a controlled value in the current available option set and reconcile removed/disabled options in the host; the component does not automatically repair a stale selection.

Update value when accepting onValueChange. If stable native-form naming is needed, serialize the selected value explicitly in the host: this API does not expose name, form or required, and its internal generated radio name is not a product field contract.
Use the radio-group selection for a related choice and implement any associated view or data change in the host. Do not assume tabs, tabpanels, routing, readOnly or validation semantics are supplied.
Use input-group tokens for owned styles, retain native radio keyboard focus, and preserve size metrics when theme or mode changes.

limitations: The public API has no readOnly, name, form, required or invalid prop. Disabled is not a substitute for a focusable read-only contract.
The initial local selection is not recomputed just because options or defaultValue change later; the host must reconcile dynamic option sets.
The keyboard story is a bounded native-radio assertion, not a full tab-widget or native-form acceptance suite.

entries.name: Select
entries.summary: A single-value picker with grouped options, optional icons, descriptions, and native form integration.

document.purpose: Choose one stable string value from a supplied option set using a form-compatible popup listbox.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Select and DirectionProvider, with local controlled/uncontrolled adapters and shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Single selection and independent popup-open state adapters
Base UI form/keyboard/dismissal delegation
Option grouping, descriptions, selected display and empty option state
host: Valid stable option identities and accessible names
Controlled value/open updates and application validation
Application effects of a selected value

requirements.statement: Display the supplied value or local defaultValue, defaulting to the empty string. Pass an empty selected string to Base UI as null and translate a null value callback back to the empty string.
Resolve open independently from value using open or internal state initialized by defaultOpen. Update internal state only when open is undefined and forward onOpenChange as a boolean notification.
Pass name, form, autoComplete, readOnly and resolved required/disabled into Base UI Select.Root for its form-compatible input behavior.

Use Base UI Trigger/List/Item/Popup to delegate typeahead, Arrow/Home/End navigation, option activation, Escape dismissal and focus return. The keyboard story specifically exercises ArrowDown/Enter selection and trigger focus return.
Delegate disabled controls, disabled options and readOnly selection locking to Base UI. readOnly is not a promise that the popup cannot open or be browsed; it prevents value changes.
Apply the standalone label or Field/explicit label references to the trigger; associate optional descriptions to their options using ids derived from the resolved control id and encoded option value.
Render distinct option group labels in first-occurrence group order. With no options, render a disabled No options available item rather than a selectable fallback.
Use the explicit dir when supplied or the inherited Base UI direction, and render the popup through a portal with token-backed offset and collision padding.

Provide unique nonempty option value strings, meaningful labels, and values that correspond to the available option set. Empty string is reserved for no selection; the wrapper does not validate or repair duplicate, empty or unknown option identities.

When controlling value or open, update the corresponding prop from its callback. Own validation/error messages and the application action caused by a selection; the wrapper does not save or fetch records.
Provide a visible label, enclosing Field or explicit aria-label/aria-labelledby for the trigger. Do not use placeholder or the generic option-list fallback name as the control name.
Use the input group for Select-owned styles and fixed geometry, preserve Base UI focus guards and portal behavior, and keep control metrics consistent across all four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: This is a single-string selection contract, not free-text entry, multi-selection or an action-menu contract.
Base UI behavior is delegated; this record and its linked checks do not certify every browser, form reset or assistive-technology combination.
onOpenChange and onValueChange expose values only; the wrapper does not expose the primitive event-details cancellation API through those callbacks.

entries.summary: A binary on/off control for a setting, with a label that remains stable across states.

document.purpose: Present a named on/off setting with Base UI switch semantics and optional native form participation.
anatomy: native form input managed by Base UI
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Switch rendered as a native button with shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Boolean checked state delegation and callback forwarding
Switch semantics, thumb state and native-form attributes
Label/help association and disabled/readOnly delegation
host: Meaning, timing and persistence of the setting
Controlled updates and application error handling
Accessible name and form submission policy

requirements.statement: Pass checked, defaultChecked and onCheckedChange directly to Base UI Switch.Root. Expose boolean on/off state; no indeterminate state is part of the public Switch API.
Render the primitive root as a native button and forward the public ref and supported remaining button props to that button.
Retain Base UI/native-button activation for the switch. The ImmediateSetting story exercises a click followed by Space; the story description also documents Enter activation.
Pass resolved disabled and readOnly to Base UI so unavailable controls and focusable non-editable controls remain distinct states. Do not implement a separate local toggle that bypasses those props.
Forward name, value, form and resolved required to the primitive input integration. The documented form behavior includes the checked state when a name is provided.

Associate the optional visible label with the resolved control id; merge the optional description with caller and Field descriptions. Forward explicit label/invalid references through useFieldControl.

When supplying checked, update it from onCheckedChange when accepting the requested change. Own persistence, rejected updates and user feedback; switching the visual control does not perform a network save.
Provide a persistent name describing the setting through label, Field or an accessible name on the button. Do not depend on the thumb position alone to communicate meaning.
Own validation messages and native-form submission behavior. required and invalid are metadata; the switch does not determine whether the setting is permitted or save its value.
Keep switch-owned styling and fixed defaults in the input group, preserve keyboard focus visibility, and keep dimensions stable across the four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: This contract does not turn an immediate-setting presentation into automatic persistence or authorization.
Controlled/uncontrolled form behavior is delegated to Base UI; there is no additional Aegis reset handler or mixed-state model here.
Linked story assertions cover a small interaction fixture and are not certification of every form, keyboard or assistive-technology case.

requirements.statement: Own activeId and update it in response to onNavigate after performing the intended route or view transition. Navigation items are buttons, not href links; the component does not integrate a router or browser history.

When search is visible, wire onSearch to a real search interface. The displayed Cmd-K hint is visual content only; the host must register and scope any keyboard shortcut.

limitations: No router, Cmd-K listener, responsive modal drawer or automatic route-heading focus is implemented.

requirements.statement: Forward the supported Root props, including open/defaultOpen and onOpenChange, to Base UI. The wrapper does not maintain a separate open-state copy or expose event details in the typed onOpenChange callback.

Render the supplied trigger through Primitive.Trigger and use the primitive popup/close model for activation, Escape and dismissal. The scrollable-body story checks Escape close and return to the trigger.

Name the popup and body from title when supplied, otherwise from label, default Details. When showHeader is false, retain title and description in visually hidden elements and preserve their ARIA references.

On opening, choose the first visible eligible button, link, input, select, textarea or tabindex=0 descendant, excluding the scroll body itself and hidden/inert/aria-hidden ancestors; fall back to the primitive default focus behavior.
Allow primitive final focus unless the current active element is already outside the popup and is not the body; preserve a deliberate external focus handoff rather than always refocusing the trigger.

showClose renders a Primitive.Close with the accessible name Close popover, including a floating close button when the header is hidden. PopoverClose forwards primitive props/ref; deprecated asChild requires one valid React element or throws.
Render children in a separately focusable scrolling region, with optional header and footer outside that scroll container so body scrolling does not move those regions.
Portal the popup and position it with side/align and token-backed offset/collision padding. Apply optional width while CSS constrains the popup to available viewport dimensions.
When controlling open, update it from onOpenChange. Own content state, asynchronous actions, validation, submission and dirty-draft policy; a close request does not save or reset application data.

Supply a usable named trigger that accepts the primitive props/ref and a meaningful title or label. Children containing forms or interactive controls must provide their own form associations, names and disabled/readOnly states.

Use the surface group for popover-owned styles and fixed defaults, preserve nested shared-component styling and primitive focus guards, and retain keyboard-visible focus across the four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: The generic fallback label Details supplies a name but does not establish meaningful product context.
Root open props are forwarded, but Popup initialFocus/finalFocus are owned by this wrapper rather than exposed as public override props.
Popover has no component-level disabled/readOnly or native form field value. Its trigger and nested controls own those semantics.
The linked scrolling/Escape story is a scoped check, not certification of every nested popup, modal configuration or custom trigger.

requirements.statement: Resolve open from the supplied prop or local state initialized from defaultOpen. Update local state only when open is undefined and notify onOpenChange with the requested boolean.

For overlay mode, use a modal Dialog with Portal, Backdrop and Popup. For docked mode, use a nonmodal root and conditionally render an aside in place, without the overlay portal/backdrop; docked mode disables pointer dismissal.

The header close button requests false. Overlay Escape and outside-pointer behavior are delegated to Dialog, with disablePointerDismissal forwarded; docked content closes on an unprevented Escape bubbling inside the aside, not on an outside pointer.

Associate the sheet with its title and optional description ids. Render the body as a focusable region named by the title; use Dialog title/description parts in overlay mode and native heading/paragraph elements when docked.
On overlay opening, request initial focus on the first sheet icon button, normally Close. On closing, allow primitive focus return unless focus has already moved to an element outside the popup.

Docked content does not automatically focus a close control or trap focus. On unmount, restore the remembered connected opener only when focus was still inside the panel and has not already moved elsewhere.

Keep header and optional footer outside the body scroll region. headerActions takes precedence over the backward-compatible actions alias; Section and Field helpers render content structure without application data behavior.

Show navigation when both position and total are supplied. Disable Previous without its callback or at position <= 1, and Next without its callback or at position >= total; announce the position text through a polite live span.

When resizable is enabled, expose a labeled vertical separator with current/min/max values. Pointer dragging and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight change width, Shift uses the larger step, and Home/End select the measured limits; clamp width to configured and available space.

Update controlled open and record-navigation props from callbacks. Own record retrieval, loading/errors, unsaved-change policy, form submission and draft persistence across conditional mounting or closing; the sheet does not save records or veto closure for dirty forms.

Supply a meaningful title and closeLabel, valid one-based navigation position/total, and a usable trigger when needed. Custom trigger elements must preserve the primitive ref and event props; content controls require their own labels and form semantics.

Keep sheet-owned styling and fixed defaults in the surface group, preserve nested shared component ownership, respect reduced motion, and retain keyboard-visible focus and the scoped scroll container.

document.purpose: Edit the shared WorkRecord filter model and expose density and column-view controls, either inline or alongside a host-owned filter panel.
document.behaviorProvider: Aegis recordFilterReducer and controlled host state, composed from shared Base UI-backed controls.

component: translate filter edits to reducer transitions
maintain picker draft and optional internal density
applied summaries and removal focus handoff
host: own accepted RecordFilterState and apply it to records
render and control any external panel

requirements.statement: All filter edits derive a next RecordFilterState from the current value through recordFilterReducer and emit onValueChange; the bar keeps no authoritative filter-value copy.

Feed accepted changes back through value and apply the same state to the dataset. For WorkRecord semantics, applyRecordFilters uses OR within facets, AND across facets and rules, case-insensitive search and inclusive lastSeen time bounds; FilterBar itself does not fetch or filter rows.

The inline picker prevents native form submission, trims input and rejects blank or disabled commits. Equality choices for supported facets deduplicate facet values; other choices append a rule with an id. Successful commit clears the input and closes the picker.
Changing picker field or operator clears its input. Closing the popover alone does not explicitly reset its field, operator or draft; do not promise discard-on-dismiss behavior.
Panel mode delegates editing and visibility to the host. Supply onTogglePanel, filterPanelOpen and a matching panelId to connect the toggle with the real panel; the bar does not mount that panel.
Show applied criteria when their count is nonzero and either bar mode is active or the external panel is closed. Panel mode with an open panel suppresses this duplicate summary.

Before dispatching a chip removal initiated from its remove button, request focus on the next remove button, then the previous, then the search input. When search is visible and enabled, the final-chip fallback and Clear all can return focus to it. Clear all resets the filter model, including its relative 24-hour time range. Truthy selectionActions hides search while applied summaries may remain, so those search-focus requests do not guarantee recovery after the focused removal control disappears.
Truthy selectionActions hides the normal search/filter row while keeping it mounted. Applied summaries follow their own visibility rules and are not automatically removed by selection mode.

density is controlled when supplied; otherwise an internal default density is updated. Every density activation emits onDensityChange when present. The host must use that density to affect its actual rows.

columns describes host-owned visibility; onColumnVisibilityChange must update the dataset and fed-back column settings. The bar disables choices marked non-hideable or lacking a change callback; it does not itself ensure a data column remains visible.

disabled is forwarded to search, time range, picker trigger/fields, panel toggle, density buttons, column-settings trigger and removable summaries. Column checkboxes in an already-open popover use their own hideable/callback conditions; disabled does not uniformly lock those mounted choices.
Use filtering group tokens for the bar and picker layout while preserving nested control token ownership and shared keyboard, popover dismissal and focus behavior.

limitations: This record-specific filter editor is distinct from the experimental FilteredDataset composition contract.
Search and time-range changes emit immediately; the picker Apply button commits one criterion, not a global deferred filter transaction.
No remote query service, saved-filter persistence or automatic dataset wiring is provided.
The disabled prop does not disable every child in an already-open column settings popover; hosts needing a complete interaction lock must account for that limitation.

In selection mode, the search input is hidden but applied-filter controls may remain visible. Clear all or the last-chip removal can remove the focused control without a visible focus fallback; hosts must review and provide focus recovery for that composition.

document.purpose: Enter and remove multiple free-text values with atomic per-value validation and controlled host confirmation.
invariants: A committed value is trimmed, Unicode NFC normalized and nonempty. Duplicate identity uses JavaScript lowercase after normalization.
Enter or Add commits; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Blur commitment is off unless explicitly configured.
Newlines and tabs separate batch values. Commas remain literal unless comma is explicitly a commit key.
Every invalid batch is atomic: no values change and the exact submitted draft remains editable, including line breaks.
Duplicate reject is the default. Explicit ignore skips duplicates and announces their count.
Blank commit is a no-op. Validator accepts null/undefined; a nonempty string rejects; exceptions and other return types reject safely. Validators are synchronous.
In values confirmation mode a draft clears only when the host echoes the ordered requested values. This mode suits synchronous parents.

Asynchronous parents use request confirmation: accepted acknowledgment must match requestId AND requested ordered values; rejected acknowledgment preserves the draft. Stale acknowledgments never settle a newer request.
The host owns committed values and must honor the supplied AbortSignal when work is cancelled. This component cannot undo an authoritative stale host write.
Editing and restoring draft text still counts as a new draft. A delayed acceptance does not clear newer edits or steal focus.
Pending controls block additional mutations; draft remains editable. Keep editing aborts the pending request.
IME composition, native isComposing and keyCode229 prevent commit/removal. Holding Backspace does not remove values.
Empty-input Backspace arms removal; a second distinct press removes. Escape, blur or editing cancels the arm.
Suggestions are named buttons, preserve unrelated draft, and never restrict free-text entry. This is not a combobox.
Removal controls have accessible names; disabled state prevents user mutations.
document.behaviorProvider: native-textarea-plus-existing-components
document.asyncHostRequirement: Use confirmationMode=request and correlate acknowledgment IDs; discard results whose request signal is aborted.
